four months ago I bet on FurtherAI. here’s why I think more people should be paying attention! the pitch is simple: insurance companies run on workflows that are still done by hand. reading documents, pulling data, filling spreadsheets, comparing one file against another. FurtherAI builds the AI that actually does that work, end to end, in the messy real-world conditions these teams operate in. not a demo. production, every day, for companies that can’t afford to get it wrong. What's holding back large-scale AI deployments? The short answer: Architecture. At Insurtech Insights , we dug into this topic with Arron Lamp CIO of Tokio Marine HCC 's Public Risk Group - one of the hardest environments in insurance to deploy AI at scale: ↳ 15 lines of business ↳ Large, complex, unusual risks ↳ Policies that are public, so every decision gets scrutinized If you can make AI work here, you can make it work practically anywhere. Something he said stuck with me: "𝗜 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 FurtherAI , 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝘆 FurtherAI ." It's a whole philosophy. Don't burn time rebuilding what you can buy. Invest in your real value — your data and your business logic — and partner with the best to do the rest. Then keep the partner earning it: more accuracy, less cost, every year. We compiled the rest of the lessons on building scalable AI architecture into a detailed blog. Link in the first comment. Thank you Arron for being generous with your time, and Insurtech Insights for the opportunity. ...more ...more

Exciting News: McGowan Excess & Casualty , known for disciplined risk selection and responsive service to its broker partners, has selected FurtherAI to power the next phase of its underwriting operations! With FurtherAI 's agentic workspace, McGowan is automating submission intake and triage — extracting data from ACORDs, loss runs, SOVs, and supplemental applications directly into its rating workbooks. By compressing the time between submission and quote, underwriters can spend more of their day on risk analysis and pricing decisions rather than data entry, helping McGowan respond faster to brokers without compromising underwriting discipline. The platform also ingests and applies carrier guidelines at the point of clearance, surfacing appetite fit, underlying limit adequacy, and missing information earlier in the workflow — so submissions that move forward are cleaner and declinations happen sooner. " FurtherAI has been a great tool. It allowed to map our current process and autofill our workbooks, process various carrier guidelines and allowed us to really get through a ton of information and uncover additional information that you need to underwrite." — Steve Wentz McGowan Excess & Casualty Here’s to pushing the industry, Further. ...more ...more

Scaling AI adoption in insurance is different than any other industry. Arron Lamp explains it best: "If I don't have trustability, if I don't have verifiability, if I can't have something I can put in front of my compliance officer and say, ''We're using AI in our process,'' and have an audit log, I can't use it." When Arron was evaluating AI partners, FurtherAI stood out from the rest. Here’s what he had to say: "They're the only vendor we evaluated that gave us the speed, accuracy, 100%. With no prep, literally no prep. We showed up to our second round saying, ''We want you to do this.'' And they said, ''Actually, we gave you IDs. Why don't you do it?'' Nobody did that." Our Co-Founder and CEO Aman Gour sat down with Arron at InsurTech Insights to talk about how insurance teams should approach AI implementation: "Focus a little bit more on preparing for AI rather than doing AI. Spending time on that will pay huge dividends as you go forward." Full conversation linked in comments!

I'm thrilled to be wrapping up my first week here at FurtherAI ! Insurance professionals are some of the most resilient, hard-working, customer-obsessed people I know. Our industry requires us to understand nuanced regulations, risk exposures, market shifts, and coverage details, all while being product consultants, negotiators, and sometimes even cosplaying as a therapist. So why, then, are some insurance offices still relying on outdated software, filling out ACORD forms by hand, and having to "Print" Word documents just to convert them into PDFs (iykyk)? It's clear this is becoming a pressing issue for everyday producers and executives alike. AI adoption is no longer on the horizon, it's here today. A broker who used to pump out 10 quotes a day now has the capability to pump out 10 in an hour. An underwriter no longer needs to review 50 separate property and LHR documents, they can now get a comprehensive report that tells them whether a policy is worth the risk for the carrier. AI isn't replacing producers, underwriters, claims adjusters, etc.. Licenses, regulations, and the overall need for a human touchpoint make that impossible. But the organizations winning right now are the ones using AI to empower their team members, not replace them. This is why FurtherAI's mission is personal to me. I've seen firsthand how much the insurance industry, both insurers and insureds, needs this shift. A heartfelt thank you to my Zurich Simon State Farm team. You guys know how much you mean to me, both professionally and personally. To my new team at FurtherAI, let's build 🚀 🚀 🚀

Every frontier model is close to unbeatable at writing code, because code is the cleanest training data that has ever existed. Every repository has been tagged, structured, and made public. Underwriting has none of that. Joe Schmidt IV is a Partner at Andreessen Horowitz and a board member at FurtherAI. He's a licensed insurance agent and has spent over a decade in insurance. "Code has been perfectly tagged. It's a very clean data set. When it comes down to underwriting, there's a lot of proprietary data that the models don't have access to. And when it comes down to claims, there's a lot of data that they don't have access to." That data isn't sitting in a warehouse waiting to be pointed at a model. It gets created in the insurance work itself, which is why we build on the path of existing workflows rather than around it: → Submission intake, where the risk first enters the building → Underwriting notes, where judgment gets recorded → Claims files, where the outcome finally shows up A model that has never seen how your underwriters price a risk cannot learn to price it, and the only way it ever sees that is if something is capturing the decision as it happens. Thank you Joe Schmidt and Andreessen Horowitz for the conversation. Full episode linked in comments.
